newsitem.title: USA: U.S. critical of Singapore leader's voter warning.
newsitem.headline: U.S. critical of Singapore leader's voter warning.

text.p: The United States criticised Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on Tuesday for warning voters that their neighbourhoods would become slums if they elected opposition candidates in voting on Jan. 2.

Goh said on Sunday he would respect the voters' choice if they elected someone from the opposition, but, he added: "Then you'll be left behind; then in 20, 30 years' time, the whole of Singapore will be bustling away and your estate, through your own choice, will be left behind. They become slums. That's my message."

"We understand that ruling party candidates, including the prime minister, have warned that constituencies that elect opposition candidates will receive low priority in extensive government plans to upgrade public housing facilities," the State Department said.

"We believe that voters everywhere should be able to vote without fear of repercussions from government as a result of their responsibilities as citizens," a department press officer, Sharon Bowman, said in reply to a question.

Goh's ruling People's Action Party (PAP), which has run Singapore since 1959, swept back to power on Monday before a single vote was cast. Candidate nominations closed with opposition parties challenging only 36 of the 83 Parliament seats up for grabs, leaving the government a clear majority.
Before nominations wound up, government ministers delivered a stark message -- vote for the opposition and forget any prospect of getting lavish government renovation and development programmes.
